chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the slaughtered meat of the Murji'ite and the Haruriyya, so he said: 'Eat, and be decisive and steady, until what is to happen happens.'

key_terms.مَا يَكُونُ: What is to happen (referring to the rise of Al-Qaim)

ai.seo_question: Is the meat of Murji'ites and Haruriyya permissible to eat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirms the permissibility of consuming the meat of the Murji'ites and Haruriyya, emphasizing that their theological deviations do not invalidate their ritual slaughter. The phrase 'qirra wa istaqirra' is interpreted by Shia scholars as an exhortation to remain steadfast and decisive in faith, awaiting the ultimate vindication of the Ahl al-Bayt with the rise of Al-Qaim (the Mahdi). This ruling highlights the distinction between theological error and ritual purity in early Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(The narrator) says, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a slaughter of the Murjiite, and the Harouriyya.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eat, and be decisive and steady, until it happens what is going to happen (Rising of Al-Qaim<sup>asws</sup>)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about an animal slaughtered by a person of al- Murji’ah people or al-Harawriy people. He (the Imam) said, ‘You can use it for food, remain determined and firm until it happens what has to happen (reappearance of al-Mahdi with divine authority and power).’”
